address: 2855 Stevens Creek Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95050
w: The Taiwanese soup-dumpling juggernaut's Valley Fair flagship, where you can watch the pleating line fold the 18-fold xiao long bao that release a scalding pork-and-crab broth; get them with the truffle upgrade and a side of green beans.
sources: yelp.com/biz/din-tai-fung-santa-clara-5 - 2855 Stevens Creek Blvd, Westfield Valley Fair; updated July 2026, open

address: 2855 Stevens Creek Blvd, Unit A268, Santa Clara, CA 95050
w: The viral Chinese chain built on a single dish: suan cai yu, boneless fish poached in a tangy house-fermented sauerkraut and pork-bone broth. This Valley Fair location is its second Bay Area outpost, opened spring 2026.
sources: yelp.com Tai Er Sichuan Cuisine Valley Fair - opened Westfield Valley Fair spring 2026; also westfield.com/valleyfair restaurant listing, open

address: 1067 N San Antonio Rd, Los Altos, CA 94022
w: The definitive Silicon Valley Chinese institution, run by chef Lawrence Chu since 1970 and a stop for heads of state and tech elite; the minced-squab lettuce cups and lemon chicken are the enduring classics.
sources: kqed.org/checkplease/6741/chef-chus-restaurant-info - KQED Check, Please! Bay Area listing
yelp.com/biz/chef-chus-los-altos - 1067 N San Antonio Rd, updated 2026, open since 1970

w: A big banquet hall on Story Road doing weekend push-cart dim sum from a roomy second floor; go for the plump-shrimp har gow, siu mai and BBQ-pork buns rolled out on the carts.
sources: Metroactive Dining | Dynasty Chinese Seafood Restaurant — https://www.metrosiliconvalley.com/papers/metro/10.17.02/dining-0242.html (won Metro reader vote for dim sum)

address: 1698 Hostetter Rd, Ste E, San Jose, CA 95131
w: The SV-beloved individual-hot-pot chain where everyone gets their own bubbling clay pot; the House Special stone-bowl broth comes loaded with fish tofu, pork, clams and enoki, with a soft egg cracked in tableside.
sources: yelp.com/biz/boiling-point-san-jose - 1698 Hostetter Rd Ste E; updated August 2026, open (note: the former Cupertino Vallco location is permanently closed)

w: The successor brand to Little Sheep, built on a mineral-rich Mongolian broth simmered with goji, jujube and dozens of spices; order the thin-sliced lamb shoulder to swish through the milky pot.
sources: yelp.com/biz/happy-lamb-hot-pot-cupertino-3 - 19062 Stevens Creek Blvd; updated July 2026, open

w: Michelin Bib Gourmand casual offshoot from James Beard-nominated chef Tony Xu; the dan dan noodles arrive under a slick of chili oil, ground pork and mouth-numbing Sichuan peppercorn, alongside spicy wontons.
sources: MICHELIN Guide Bib Gourmand (Mian, first location); Cupertino outpost at 19389 Stevens Creek Blvd

w: A Cupertino Taiwanese comfort-food anchor since 1982; the flagship beef noodle soup pairs braised beef and tendon with hand-pulled noodles in a rich broth, backed by spicy red-oil mini wontons.
sources: yelp.com/biz/liangs-village-cupertino - 20530 Stevens Creek Blvd; updated May 2026, open

w: A tiny family-run kitchen tucked in a Branham Lane strip mall turning out some of the South Bay's most authentic Sichuan home cooking, heavy on mala seasoning, dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorn in unfussy portions.
sources: yelp.com/biz/yummy-kitchen-san-jose - 1711 Branham Ln, filed under Szechuan; updated July 2026, open

w: A Milpitas Shanghainese room going 15-plus years; the xiao long bao are praised for juicy filling and a delicate skin, alongside drunken chicken and stir-fried eel.
sources: yelp.com/biz/shanghai-delight-milpitas-3 - 218 Barber Ct; updated August 2026, open

w: A downtown Castro Street newcomer doing Shanghai-style dumplings and noodles; the pork-belly xiao long bao come with a flavorful broth trapped inside a hand-pleated skin.
A West San Jose Sichuan spot near the Cupertino line known for face-melting mala; the boiled fish in chili oil and the mapo tofu bring the numbing-spicy Chengdu heat.
sources: yelp.com/biz/shang-cafe-san-jose-3 - 6154 Bollinger Rd, filed under Szechuan; updated June 2026, open

address: 10911 N Wolfe Rd, Ste B, Cupertino, CA 95014
w: KQED's pick for the South Bay's tastiest roast duck, open late (till midnight most nights) from the team behind next-door banquet hall Jade Tea Garden; the lacquered Cantonese roast duck is the must-order, alongside Hunan rice noodles.
sources: kqed.org/arts/13991068 - Luke Tsai, 'A Cupertino Noodle House Slings the South Bay's Tastiest Roast Duck'; 10911 N Wolfe Rd Ste B

w: An authentic Shaanxi/Xi'an kitchen in Milpitas specializing in wide, hand-ripped biang biang noodles slicked with chili oil, plus rou jia mo (Chinese 'burger') and cumin-lamb dishes.
sources: yelp.com/biz/xian-kitchen-milpitas-5 - 300 Barber Ct; updated August 2026, open

w: A packed Sunnyvale specialist in Shanxi-style noodles; the dao xiao mian (knife-shaved noodles) are shaved to order into soups that are soft yet chewy, with salt-and-pepper eggplant on the side.
sources: yelp.com/biz/xiang-xiang-noodle-sunnyvale - 1115 Tasman Dr #2228; updated July 2026, open

address: 5152 Moorpark Ave, Ste 30, San Jose, CA 95129
w: A West San Jose Hunan kitchen bringing Changsha-style dry heat; the house smoked pork tossed with dried chilies and scallions arrives in a flaming pot, distinct from the numbing mala of Sichuan.
sources: yelp.com/biz Hunan Impression San Jose - 5152 Moorpark Ave Ste 30; Hunan cuisine, open

address: 19409 Stevens Creek Blvd, Ste 100, Cupertino, CA 95014
w: The global Sichuan hot-pot chain famous for over-the-top service and a huge sauce bar; get the split pot with the mala Sichuan broth, an extensive-menu sauce bar, and the theatrical hand-pulled-noodle dance.
sources: yelp.com/biz/haidilao-hot-pot-cupertino-4 - 19409 Stevens Creek Blvd Ste 100; updated August 2026, open

w: A Milpitas individual-hot-pot shop with a dozen personal-pot flavors; the Taiwanese Supreme broth comes packed with fish balls, pork and greens, a solo alternative to Boiling Point.
sources: yelp.com/biz/tasty-pot-milpitas-2 - 222 Barber Ct; updated July 2026, open

w: A Milpitas Cantonese BBQ-and-dim-sum spot whose roast duck and roast pork hang in the window; also strong on Chiu Chow dumplings and daily dim sum plates.
sources: yelp.com/biz/cheung-hing-milpitas-milpitas - 1235 E Calaveras Blvd, filed under Dim Sum; updated July 2026, open

w: A small downtown-Sunnyvale Hunan room for chili-forward, smoky Changsha cooking; the smoked pork and steamed fish head with chopped chilies deliver Hunan's dry, punchy heat.
sources: yelp.com/biz/hunan-house-sunnyvale-2 - 122 S Sunnyvale Ave; updated July 2026, open
